_policy: Pre-registered targets for the #4234 round (the phase arbiter's 32-beat guard), frozen BEFORE any arm was scored live, in the shape of q4163_arbiter_frozen.json: numbers below are read from the baseline root (the shipped behavior); arms are selected on the TUNE halves and the holdout is read once on the chosen arm.
issue: Most off-beat grids at the right tempo are off-beat from acquisition and never moved, not wrong flips (finding #4369): tune T-level grids on the half-beat, Harmonix 7 of 122, Ballroom 31 of 220 (beat F ~0). On them the union's events favor the beat by ~1.5-2:1, under the 32-beat guard's 2:1 ratio and .3 on-grid share, which #4160 chose on kicks alone. The return path and the minimum event count #4234 was filed with forecast no gain (return path +0/-2 on both sets; a 16-event minimum -20 Ballroom tracks) and were dropped with Kevin's OK (2026-10-21).
mechanism_evidence: finding #4370: the arbiter replayed from the instrumented beat sidecar (window pushes + votes) matches the shipped scheduler exactly (604 tracks, 130,004 votes); as a 2-state machine on the recorded grid, tune forecasts: long ratio 1.5 / share .4: Harmonix +.0063 (+9/-4), Ballroom +.0172 (+14/-1); + streak 3: +.0174 (+15/-4), +.0201 (+16/-2); long ratio 1.33 / share .5 / streak 3: +.0124 (+15/-6), +.0206 (+18/-3); batida flat or up, ambient 0 shifts. Live knob binary vs forecast on the 24 most-moved tune tracks: 21 within .1 beat F, the other 3 in the forecast's direction. Losses are the #4167 syncopated population (kicks on the 'and' just under 2:1: 0035, 0164, 0599, 0569, Latin_Jam5-12).
design_constraint: Only PhaseArbiterCfg's long_ratio (new field, shipped 2.0 = the short ratio), long_share and streak change. Evidence streams, event threshold, the 8-beat window and its 2:1 ratio, tolerance, PLL, estimator and scheduler stay as shipped. The arbiter does not feed the tempo estimator, so tempo metrics are identical by construction (G1) and the wire's published bpm (published on lock) cannot change (G5 publish).

targets.P1_ballroom: ballroom holdout beat_f >= baseline + 0.010 (half the tune forecast of the chosen point)
targets.P2_harmonix: harmonix holdout beat_f >= baseline + 0.008 (half the tune forecast)
targets.P3_flips: on harmonix and ballroom holdout, the tracks that LOSE more than 0.1 beat_f number fewer than those that GAIN more than 0.1 (the losses are the #4167 syncopated population; the round must win more grids than it breaks)
targets.G1_tempo_identical: acc1, acc2, no_est on all three datasets IDENTICAL to baseline (the arbiter does not feed the estimator; any difference is a bug, not a tolerance)
targets.G2_continuity: harmonix and ballroom holdout cmlt, amlt, downbeat_f each >= baseline - 0.005
targets.G3_anti_locked: harmonix holdout anti_locked <= baseline; ballroom holdout anti_locked <= baseline - 3 (the defect this round targets)
targets.G4_genres: per-genre ballroom holdout beat_f: no genre down by more than 0.02
targets.G5_negatives: 155 beatless clips: publish IDENTICAL (by construction, published on lock); beats/min <= baseline + 1.0; pulse-low third beats/min <= baseline + 1.0
targets.G6_batida: techno and house: no seed worse than baseline beat F by more than 0.02 and none newly below 0.7 from >= 0.7; other templates: beat F not worse by more than 0.01 and bpm_ratio unchanged (+-0.01) on any seed; ambient: beats fired not above baseline
targets.G7_structure_drop: harmonix all: drop hit_rate >= baseline - 0.01, false_drops_per_min <= baseline + 0.02, predict_drop false_alarms_per_min <= baseline + 0.05, coverage at 0.5 / 0.8 each >= baseline - 0.01, boundary_3_0s f >= baseline - 0.005
targets.G8_fixture: bench/check_fixture.py passes on the final binary (knobs removed)
targets.G9_build: cargo test (default and analyze), the CI clippy sets (--all-targets for default, analyze and release) and clippy -p fosfora-app --lib --no-default-features (XR)
targets.G10_owner: Kevin listens to click-track A/B renders (bench/q4163_listen.py: same 24 s twice, base clicks then candidate clicks) of holdout tracks the verdict moved both ways, before the commit

on_miss: a missed target or guard reverts that arm, or is stated with its numbers and explicitly accepted by Kevin; never silently
